concurrency.note: The gate was inert before this branch: -race passed from the day it was written because no test ran two operations at once. The hammer tests in memory and hosted are what make this result mean anything. It found its first real defect immediately after they landed -- an unsynchronised counter in a new test's own fixture.

mutation.note: No mutation-score tool was run, and this is deliberately not recorded as a score. What was done instead is the targeted form the TDD policy accepts: for each confirmed finding the fix was reverted (or the original defect reinstated) and the test re-run to confirm it goes red for the stated reason. That is a mutant placed exactly where it matters, rather than a percentage over arbitrary ones.

performance.reason: No performance-affecting optimisation is included in this branch. The retrieval-quality gate (just bench-code) is the relevant regression check and matched its checked-in baseline digest on every batch: 1231205ae7a330b259fd5c172c798d6353bbd03fb557a4acd6f6126598fcc573. The performance findings the audit raised are recorded as open entries in HARDENING.md, each to be taken behind a benchstat comparison rather than folded in here.
